get.description: Lists the API tokens (never their values), in their brief view by default.

post.description: Creates an API token, with a random value or the one given (32 alphanumeric characters). The value is in the answer, and ONLY in that answer: Netshot only keeps a hash of it, so it can't be read afterwards.

get.description: Gets an API token, without its value.

delete.description: Deletes an API token, which can't authenticate anymore.

get.description: Gets the principal the request is authenticated as: kind USER for the user of a session or of a JWT access token, API_TOKEN for an API token (which has no user name), with the authentication method, the permission level and its role.

patch.description: Changes the password of the current user, who must be a local user (not an API token, nor a user authenticated by an identity provider). The current password must be given, and the new one must comply with the password policy (400 otherwise).

get.description: Gets the session identified by the session cookie: its user, when it was created and its idle timeout. Answers 401 if the request is not authenticated, and 404 if it is authenticated otherwise than by a session (API token, JWT access token): use GET /auth/me for the principal of any request.

post.description: Logs in with a username and a password, or an OIDC authorization code with its redirect URI, and creates a session: the session cookie is set in the response, and the previous session of the client (if any) is dropped. Answers 201 with the session. A wrong user name, password or code is a 401. An expired password is a 403 (give a newPassword to change it while logging in); a new password which does not comply with the password policy is a 400. Useless when using API tokens.

delete.description: Terminates the session identified by the session cookie. Always answers 204, even without a session (the operation is idempotent). For a user who logged in through an identity provider (not a local user), when OIDC is available, the X-OIDC-EndSessionEndpoint header gives the IdP endpoint the client can send the user to, to end the session there too.

get.description: Counts the compliance results matching the filters of the list, by the values of up to two fields (groupBy: result, policy, rule, device, group, domain) and/or by time bucket (interval: hour, day, week or month, on checkDate, from/to, timeZone). A result is counted once per group of its device.

Lists the results of the last compliance checks, one per device and rule (a rule never checked on a device has no result here), with the exemption of the device from the rule. Filters: device, deviceName, domain and group (of the device), rule, ruleName, policy, policyName, result, checkDate, exemptionExpirationDate; q searches the device, rule and policy names.

get.summary: List the compliance results of a device
get.description: Lists the rules of the policies applying to a device (through its groups) with the result of their last check (none if never checked) and the exemption of the device. (unlike the list across devices, which only has the checked ones). Filters: rule, ruleName, policy, policyName, result, checkDate, exemptionExpirationDate.
Lists the hardware compliance rules, in their brief view by default.

put.description: Replaces the definition of a hardware rule.

patch.description: Changes some properties of a hardware rule (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396).

get.description: Lists the compliance policies, in their brief view by default. The targetGroup filter gives the policies applying to a group.

post.description: Creates a compliance policy, without rules.

put.description: Replaces the name and the target groups of a policy. The compliance results of the devices of a group removed from the policy are deleted.

delete.description: Deletes a policy, with its rules, their exemptions and results.

patch.description: Changes some properties of a policy (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396).

get.summary: List the rules of a policy
get.description: Lists the rules of a policy, as the rule list filtered on the policy (same parameters).
Lists the compliance rules of all the policies, in their brief view by default (the type, TEXT, JAVASCRIPT or PYTHON, tells which other properties a rule has).

post.description: Creates a rule in a policy (required). A script rule without script gets the template script; the rule is disabled unless enabled is true.

put.description: Replaces the definition of a rule (its type and its policy can't change; its exemptions are unchanged).

delete.description: Deletes a rule, with its exemptions and results.

patch.description: Changes some properties of a rule (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396).

get.summary: List the exemptions of a rule
get.description: Lists the devices exempted from a rule, with the date their exemption ends. Filters: device, expirationDate.

put.summary: Replace the exemptions of a rule
put.description: Replaces the whole set of devices exempted from a rule (an empty list removes them all), and answers the new set.

post.description: Checks a rule definition (which isn't stored) against a device, without any side effect, and answers the result, with what the check logged. A device without configuration gives a NOTAPPLICABLE result.

get.description: Lists the software compliance rules, in the order they are checked in by default (priority is the position of the rule, from 1).

post.description: Creates a software rule, at the given priority (position) or as the last one.

put.description: Replaces the definition of a software rule. A priority moves the rule to that position (the other rules shift); without priority the rule keeps its position.

delete.description: Deletes a software rule (the rules after it move up).

patch.description: Changes some properties of a software rule (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396), possibly its priority (position).

get.description: Gets a configuration with its attributes. The long texts and files are not inlined: the attributes give the url to download them.

get.summary: Compare a configuration with another one
get.description: Compares the configuration (the revised one) with another one (the original one, given by with, by default the one gathered just before it on the same device, or an empty configuration if it is the first). The configurations must be of the same type of device. The configurations are written in their brief view unless expanded (expand=original,revised).

parameters.name: with
parameters.description: ID of the configuration to compare with (the original one)

get.summary: Download an item of a configuration
get.description: Downloads a long text item (text/plain, UTF-8) or a file item (application/octet-stream) of a configuration, as an attachment. 404 if the configuration has no such item, or not a downloadable one (a short value), or if it has no content.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: Name of the item (an attribute of the configuration)

get.description: Counts the configurations (the configuration changes) matching the filters of the configuration list, by device and/or author (groupBy) and/or by time bucket (interval: hour, day, week or month, on changeDate, from/to, timeZone).

Lists the configurations of all the devices, in their brief view by default (device, date, author), the latest first. The attributes are only there in the full view (or with fields=attributes), and never hold the long texts and files: download them from their url. The filters on domain and group apply to the device of the configuration.

get.summary: List the configurations of a device
get.description: Lists the configurations of a device, as the configuration list filtered on the device (same parameters), the latest first.

Lists the global credential sets, in their brief view by default. The credential sets specific to a device access are left out, unless the deviceSpecific filter is given (deviceSpecific=true lists only those, deviceSpecific=false only the global ones). The secrets are never returned.

post.description: Creates a global credential set. The secrets the type needs must be given, by value or as a location in a Vault instance.

get.description: Gets a credential set. The secrets are never returned, only whether they are set.

put.description: Replaces the definition of a global credential set (its type can't change). A username, secret or Vault location left out is unchanged; a secret set to null is cleared (which the secrets the type needs refuse). With If-Match, the credential set must still be at the given version (ETag).

delete.description: Deletes a global credential set, which must not be used by any device or task. With If-Match, the credential set must still be at the given version (ETag).

patch.description: Changes some properties of a global credential set (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396). The usernames and secrets are unchanged unless the patch gives them (or a Vault location replacing them). With If-Match, the credential set must still be at the given version (ETag).

get.description: Lists the distinct device families (driver and family) of the devices, with their number of devices. An aggregate: items have no id nor url.

get.summary: List the interfaces of a device
get.description: Lists the network interfaces of a device, in their brief view by default (name, description, enabled; view=full adds the addresses). Besides the filters on the fields, ipAddress (exact or net lookup) and macAddress filter on the addresses.

get.summary: List the modules of a device
get.description: Lists the hardware modules of a device, in their brief view by default (slot, part number, serial number): the current ones only, unless removed=true, which lists the modules removed from the device (kept for the history) too, flagged removed.

Lists the devices, in their brief view by default. Besides the filters on the fields, the query parameter takes a device search query (such as [Family] is "Cisco IOS" and [Location] contains "Paris"), and group, tag and compliant filter on the group membership, the tags and the configuration compliance. Like any list, it can be exported as CSV (Accept: text/csv) or Excel (Accept: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet). With the Excel format, the include parameter writes a workbook with more sheets for the matching devices.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Device search query, in the Netshot query language

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Excel export only: the extra sheets of the workbook, among interfaces, inventory, inventoryHistory (with the removed modules), locations, compliance, groups and driverAttributes

post.description: Adds a device, asynchronously: answers 202 with the task doing the work, whose location is in the Location header. Without a driver, a task discovers the type of the device and the device is only created if the discovery succeeds (an SNMP community is needed). With a driver, the device is created immediately and a task takes its first snapshot.

post.summary: Check the compliance of a device
post.description: Creates a task which checks the configuration compliance of the device (as soon as possible by default). Answers 202 with the task, whose location is in the Location header.

put.description: Replaces the editable properties of a device (status, management address and domain, comments, tags, options, accesses). The other properties are read only and ignored. The secrets of the credential sets specific to the device which are left out are kept. With If-Match, the device must still be at the given version (ETag).

delete.description: Deletes a device, with its configurations and results. With If-Match, the device must still be at the given version (ETag).

patch.description: Changes some editable properties of a device (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396; a list such as the accesses is replaced as a whole). With If-Match, the device must still be at the given version (ETag).

get.description: Counts the devices matching the filters of the device list (and the query), by the values of up to two fields (groupBy: status, mgmtDomain, family, driver, networkClass, softwareVersion, softwareLevel, location, eolDate, eosDate, group, tag, compliant) and/or by time bucket (interval: hour, day, week or month, on createdDate, changeDate, eolDate or eosDate, from/to, timeZone).

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Device search query, in the Netshot query language

post.summary: Run the diagnostics of a device
post.description: Creates a task which runs the diagnostics of the device (as soon as possible by default). Answers 202 with the task, whose location is in the Location header.

post.summary: Run a script on a device
post.description: Creates a task which runs a script on the device (as soon as possible by default): either a saved script (savedScript), or the text of a script with the driver it is written for (script and deviceDriver). Answers 202 with the task, whose location is in the Location header.

post.summary: Take a snapshot of a device
post.description: Creates a task which takes a snapshot of the device (as soon as possible by default). Answers 202 with the task, whose location is in the Location header.

get.description: Lists the distinct tags attached to at least one device, with their number of devices. An aggregate: items have no id nor url.

Lists the device types: the device drivers loaded by the server, in their brief view by default (name, description, version). View full adds the attributes, options, accesses... Items have no id nor url: the name is what the devices refer to.
Lists the distinct part numbers of the modules, with their number of modules. An aggregate: items have no id nor url.
Lists the distinct (non empty) software versions of the devices, with their number of devices. An aggregate: items have no id nor url.
Lists the diagnostics, in their brief view by default.

post.description: Creates a diagnostic: a CLI command (SIMPLE), or a JavaScript or Python script.

put.description: Replaces the definition of a diagnostic (its type can't change). The results of the diagnostic are deleted when its target group changes.

delete.description: Deletes a diagnostic, with its results.

patch.description: Changes some properties of a diagnostic (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396).

get.summary: List the diagnostic results of a device
get.description: Lists the last result of each diagnostic run on a device, with the diagnostic as a reference.
Lists the device domains, in their brief view by default.

put.description: Replaces the definition of a domain. With If-Match, the domain must still be at the given version (ETag).

delete.description: Deletes a domain, which must not be used by any device or credential set. With If-Match, the domain must still be at the given version (ETag).

patch.description: Changes some properties of a domain (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396). With If-Match, the domain must still be at the given version (ETag).

get.description: Lists the device groups, in their brief view by default. The device filter gives the groups a device is a member of.

post.description: Creates a device group: a static group of the given devices, or a dynamic group of the devices matching the query.

put.description: Replaces the definition of a group (its type can't change; the devices of a static group are unchanged unless given). With If-Match, the group must still be at the given version (ETag).

delete.description: Deletes a group (not its devices). With If-Match, the group must still be at the given version (ETag).

patch.description: Changes some properties of a group (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396). With If-Match, the group must still be at the given version (ETag).

get.summary: List the devices of a group
get.description: Lists the devices of a group, as the device list filtered on the group (same parameters).

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Device search query, in the Netshot query language

get.description: Lists the hooks, in their brief view by default.

post.description: Creates a hook: Netshot runs its action when one of its triggers occurs (a Web hook posts the event to a URL).

put.description: Replaces the definition of a hook (its type can't change). Hooks have no version: there is no ETag.

patch.description: Changes some properties of a hook (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396; the triggers are replaced as a whole).

get.description: Lists the command scripts, in their brief view by default (without the code). The user inputs are only extracted (by evaluating the scripts) when they are asked for.

post.description: Validates and creates a command script, the author being the user.
Checks the driver, the name and the code of a script definition (by evaluating it) without saving it: 200 with the script and its user inputs, 400 with the problem otherwise.

get.summary: Probe the health of the server
get.description: Liveness and readiness probe, for load balancers and orchestrators. Not authenticated, and it gives nothing but the status (no version, no detail): 200 with status UP when all the services of the server are running and healthy, 503 with status DOWN otherwise (while starting or stopping, or when a service fails). The services are detailed by GET /system/services.

get.summary: Check whether the server is the cluster master
get.description: Gets the mastership status of the server answering, to let a load balancer send the requests to the master only. Not authenticated. Answers 200 when the server is the master (or clustering is not enabled) and 503 when it is not.
Gets the version of Netshot, the time of the server and the idle timeout of the user sessions.
Lists the members of the high availability cluster (none if clustering is not enabled), in a single page.

get.summary: List the services of the server
get.description: Lists the services of the server (task manager, Syslog server, web server...) in start order, with their state, whether they are healthy and their statistics, in a single page.

get.summary: List the tasks of a device
get.description: Lists the tasks targeting a device, as the task list filtered on the device (same parameters).

post.description: Cancels a scheduled task, or requests the cancellation of a running group task or of a device task still waiting for its device (cancelRequested). Refused (409) in any other status.

get.description: Lists the tasks, in their brief view by default, the latest first.

post.description: Creates a task and schedules it (as soon as possible by default). Answers 202 with the task, whose location is in the Location header. Running scripts needs the execute-read-write role, scanning subnets the read-write role, and purging the database the admin role.

get.summary: Get the debug log of a task
get.description: Gets the full debug log of a task run with debug enabled.

Counts the tasks matching the filters of the task list, by the values of up to two fields (groupBy: type, status, author, scheduleType, device, group, runnerId) and/or by time bucket (interval: hour, day, week or month, on executionDate (default), creationDate, changeDate or scheduleReference, from/to, timeZone). Without execution date, a task isn't counted by executionDate.

get.summary: Get the number of tasks by status
get.description: Returns the number of tasks in each status (0 included), and the number of task threads.

parameters.name: parentTask
parameters.description: Only count the child tasks of this parent task ID

get.description: Lists the Netshot users, in their brief view by default.

post.description: Creates a local user (the password is required, and must comply with the password policy) or a remote one (no password: it authenticates through RADIUS, TACACS+ or OIDC, and the user only gives it its permission level).

put.description: Replaces the definition of a user. An absent password is unchanged (it is required to make a remote user a local one). A user can't edit itself (403). Users have no version: there is no ETag.

delete.description: Deletes a user. A user can't delete itself (403).

patch.description: Changes some properties of a user (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396). The password is changed by giving one. A user can't edit itself (403).

get.description: Lists the Vault instances, in their brief view by default. The secrets are never returned.

post.description: Creates a Vault instance. The secrets required by the authentication method must be given.

get.description: Gets a Vault instance. The secrets are never returned, only whether they are set.

put.description: Replaces the definition of a Vault instance. A secret left out is unchanged; a secret set to null is cleared (which an authentication method needing it refuses). With If-Match, the Vault instance must still be at the given version (ETag).

delete.description: Deletes a Vault instance, which must not be referenced by any credential field. With If-Match, the Vault instance must still be at the given version (ETag).

patch.description: Changes some properties of a Vault instance (JSON merge patch, RFC 7396). The secrets are unchanged unless the patch gives them. With If-Match, the Vault instance must still be at the given version (ETag).

post.description: Tries to log in to a saved Vault instance, without changing anything. A failed login is a successful answer with success=false and the reason.
Tries to log in with a Vault instance definition which isn't saved (it must be complete, secrets included). A failed login is a successful answer with success=false and the reason.
